 10|
 11|이것은 오직 전설로만 전해지는 영초입니다.
 12|
 13|불로불사, 불로장생을 꿈꾸는 지배자들은 불로초를 찾기 위해 수많은 재물과 인력을 쏟아부었지만, 지금까지 그 누구도 발견하지 못했습니다.
 14|
 15|그러나 당신의 남은 수명이 천 년쯤 된다면 도전해 보는 것도 나쁘지 않습니다.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|등급 : ???
 20|
 21|제한 : 진태경
 22|
 23|임무 : 불로초 습득(미완료)
 24|
 25|보상 : ???
 26|
 27|실패 : ???
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|“안 해!”
 34|
 35|삐빅.
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|- 퀘스트를 거절하셨습니다.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|퀘스트 꼬라지 봐라. 오죽하면 퀘스트 등급도 물음표 처리가 되어 있을까.
 44|
 45|‘뭐? 남은 수명이 천 년쯤 되면 도전해 보는 것도 나쁘지 않아?’
 46|
 47|이게 말이야, 방구야.
 48|
 49|내 어이없는 눈빛에 장태보가 수염을 쓰다듬었다.
 50|
 51|“왜, 못 하겠나?”
 52|
 53|“……이걸 도대체 어떻게 합니까?”
 54|
 55|“그럼 관두게. 하수오는 돌려주고.”
 56|
 57|장태보가 내 손에서 하수오를 휙 낚아채더니 아삭아삭 씹기 시작했다.
 58|
 59|“어, 달다. 역시 오십 년 산이야.”
 60|
 61|“…….”
 62|
 63|“응? 자네들 아직도 거기 있나? 무슨 볼일이라도 있어?”
 64|
 65|“아니, 어르신.”
 66|
 67|“왜?”
 68|
 69|“불로초를 구해 오라는 게 상식적으로 말이나 됩니까?”
 70|
 71|“무림에서 상식을 따지는 놈은 오랜만에 보는군. 천년설삼도 있는데 불로초라고 없을까?”
 72|
 73|“…….”
 74|
 75|제법 그럴듯한데.
 76|
 77|순간 설득당할 뻔했지만 다시 정신을 차렸다. 이 바늘도 안 들어갈 것 같은 노인네를 어떻게든 설득해야 한다.
 78|
 79|“대신 필요하신 게 있다면 뭐든 구해 드리겠습니다. 불로초 같은 거 말고요.”
 80|
 81|“정말인가?”
 82|
 83|“그럼요. 정 안 되면 저희 가문의 힘을 총동원해서라도.”
 84|
 85|“흠. 요새 태원진가의 위세가 대단하다는 건 나도 익히 들어 알고 있지.”
 86|
 87|고개를 끄덕인 장태보가 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“그럼 목이 마르니 공청석유(空靑石油) 한 병 구해 오게.”
 90|
 91|“예?”
 92|
 93|공청석유? 한 방울이면 일 갑자의 공력을 얻는다는 그거?
 94|
 95|쌍욕이 튀어 나가려는 걸 간신히 참았다. 장태보가 실실 웃으며 말을 잇는다.
 96|
 97|“만년한철로 병기를 만든다고 했지? 그럼 검갑도 좋은 걸 써야겠구먼. 내 듣자 하니 저 세상 끝에 용이 있다던데, 발톱 좀 뽑아 오게. 겸사겸사 여의주도 하나 챙겨 오고.”
 98|
 99|띠링.
100|
101|
102|
103|- 퀘스트, [공청석유, 용의 발톱, 여의주 구하기]가 생성되었습니다.
104|
105|
106|
107|퀘스트를 수락하시겠습니까?
108|
109|Y   /   N
110|
111|
112|
113|……하겠냐?
114|
115|속이 부글부글 끓어오르는 걸 느끼며 퀘스트창을 지웠다. 혁무진이 입을 가리고 소곤거렸다.
116|
117|“노인네가 노망 난 것 같은데요?”
118|
119|“다 들린다. 대가리에 피도 안 마른 놈이 못 하는 말이 없구나.”
120|
121|장태보가 솥뚜껑만 한 주먹을 흔들던 그때, 청풍이 손을 번쩍 들고 외쳤다.
122|
123|“저 찾으러 갈래요! 저 시켜 주세요!”
124|
125|“뭐?”
126|
127|“불로초! 공청석유! 용!”
128|
129|드디어 이 구역의 미친놈이 나섰구나.
130|
131|샛별처럼 반짝이는 눈빛과 열정으로 타오르는 몸짓. 청풍의 박력에 장태보가 흠칫 물러섰다.
132|
133|“네놈은 누구냐?”
134|
135|청풍이 씩씩하게 대답했다.
136|
137|“저는 우리 할아버지 손잔데요!”
138|
139|“네놈 조부님이 누군데?”
140|
141|“우리 할아버지신데요!”
142|
143|“……미친놈이로고.”
144|
145|어서 와, 청풍은 처음이지?
146|
147|고개를 절레절레 내젓는 장태보에게 슬쩍 한마디를 던졌다.
148|
149|“혹시 매종학 대협을 아십니까?”
150|
151|“내 비록 무인은 아니나, 일평생을 무림에 발을 담그고 있던 몸일세. 백정들도 아는 검성을 모르겠나?”
152|
153|“저 친구가 그 검성이 직접 키우며 가르친 제자입니다.”
154|
155|“뭐라! 그게 사실인가?”
156|
157|“거짓말해서 뭐 하겠습니까? 그것도 검성씩이나 되는 분의 이름을 걸고.”
158|
159|“허, 검성의 후인이란 말이지…….”
160|
161|먹혔나? 원래 세상 어딜 가나 최고는 학연, 지연, 혈연이다.
162|
163|무림에서 검성 매종학의 존재는 그 자체만으로도 존경과 경의의 대상.
164|
165|사뭇 놀란 표정으로 청풍을 바라보던 장태보가 입을 열었다.
166|
167|“그래서, 뭐 어쩌라고?”
168|
169|“아…….”
170|
171|“나는 화산파와는 아무 연관도 없어. 아니, 삼십여 년 전쯤에 현 화산파 장문인인 천검진인(天劍眞人)의 부탁으로 검을 만들어 준 적이 있긴 하군. 하지만 그뿐일세.”
172|
173|단호한 목소리가 이어졌다.
174|
175|“내 나이가 팔순이야. 이만하면 몸도 정정하고 모아 놓은 재산도 많지. 쇠를 주무르던 사람으로서도 천하에서 세 손가락 안에 들었다고 자부하네.”
176|
177|“그래서 이렇게 부탁드리는 겁니다.”
178|
179|“그래서 이렇게 거절하는 거네. 내가 할 만한 일은 다 끝났어. 검은 질리도록 만들어 봤고.”
180|
181|“저는 창인데요.”
182|
183|“아, 그랬던가?”
184|
185|“예.”
186|
187|“창이라면 손이 더 가겠군. 차라리 검이 나아.”
188|
189|“어르신!”
190|
191|나는 간절한 눈빛으로 정태보의 손을 붙잡았다.
192|
193|“오랜만에 소일거리 하신다고 생각하시고 딱 한 번만 도와주시면 안 됩니까?”
194|
195|“내가 언제 안 된다고 했나?”
196|
197|“방금까지는 안 하신다면서요.”
198|
199|정태보가 모질게 손을 뿌리쳤다.
200|
201|“도와준다니까. 불로초 찾아오면.”
202|
203|“아, 제발요.”
204|
205|“겸사겸사 공청석유와 여의주도 챙겨 오고. 내 듣자 하니 용을 상대할 때는 꼬리를 피해 뒤로 돌아가서 목을 조르면 된다더군. 다치지 말라고 알려 주는 걸세.”
206|
207|“……용이 무슨 사람입니까? 목을 졸라서 죽이게?”
208|
209|“그럼 불알을 터트려.”
210|
211|“암컷이면요?”
212|
213|“다음 생에 만나세.”
214|
215|오랜만에 만난 강적이다.
216|
217|세월로 다져진 사람 엿 먹이는 화법에 주먹이 부르르 떨리고 뒷골이 당겼다.
218|
219|“이러시깁니까?”
220|
221|“이러기일세.”
222|
223|“이렇게까지 하고 싶진 않았는데…….”
224|
225|“씨부려 보게.”
226|
227|“소문내 드려요? 여기 전 철기방주가 살고 있다고?”
228|
229|말만 이렇게 하는 거지, 당연히 그럴 생각은 없다.
230|
231|하지만 장태보는 귀찮게 만들어 주겠다는 내 말에도 씨익 웃었다.
232|
233|“그럼 어쩔 수 없지. 온갖 날파리가 꼬이기 전에 철기방으로 돌아가는 수밖에.”
234|
235|“엥?”
236|
237|이게 아닌데. 그렇게 생각하던 그때 장태보가 물었다.
238|
239|“내가 철기방으로 돌아가면 뭘 할 것 같나?”
240|
241|“……저야 모르죠.”
242|
243|“내 남은 인생을 바쳐 열 개의 병장기를 만들걸세. 그렇게 심혈을 기울여 만든 병기를 구파일방의 주인들에게 하나씩 나눠 주면서 태원진가에 대해 심도 깊은 대화도 나눌 생각일세. 특히 자네 이름이 많이 나올 거야.”
244|
245|“무, 무슨 얘기를 하시려고.”
246|
247|“그걸 상상에 맡기지. 아, 참고로 무인이란 무공의 높낮이에 상관없이 병장기에 목숨도 거는 자들이란 사실은 알고 있겠지? 내 약소한 부탁 정도는 쉽게 들어줄 게 분명해.”
248|
249|“…….”
250|
251|구파일방의 장문인들에게는 약소한 부탁이겠지만 나나 태원진가 입장에서는 전혀 약소하지 않을 거다.
252|
253|그들 앞에서 몇 마디만 씹어 대도 평판 하락은 기본이요, 어쩌면 실질적인 압박이 가해질지도 모른다.
254|
255|“자, 이제 나는 떠날 준비를 해야겠군. 보자, 뭘 챙겨야 하려나…….”
256|
257|덥석. 짐을 싸기 위해 방으로 들어가려는 그의 손목을 붙잡았다. 장태보가 천연덕스럽게 묻는다.
258|
259|“왜 이러나?”
260|
261|나는 힘없이 고개를 떨궜다.
262|
263|“그만하십쇼. 제가 졌습니다.”
264|
265|“그것뿐인가?”
266|
267|“까불어서 죄송합니다.”
268|
269|“그리고?”
270|
271|“여기 계신 것에 대해서는 일절 발설하지 않겠습니다.”
272|
273|“이렇게 찾아온 걸로 봐서는 자네만 아는 사실이 아닐 텐데?”
274|
275|“저희 큰형님께도 잘 말씀드리겠습니다.”
276|
277|“틀림없겠지?”
278|
279|“물론입니다.”
280|
281|“음. 아주 싸가지 없는 놈은 아니로군.”
282|
283|원하는 대답을 모두 얻었는지 흡족하게 웃는 장태보다.
284|
285|지금까지 나보다 강한 적들을 물리쳐 왔지만 은퇴 후 한적한 노후 라이프를 즐기는 노인의 마음은 꺾지 못했다.
286|
287|‘그럼 만년한철은 어디 가서 제련해야 하나.’
288|
289|드디어 생애 처음으로 애병이라는 게 생기나 싶었는데…….
290|
291|막막해진 심정으로 반쯤 씹히다가 버려진 하수오를 바라보던 그때였다.
292|
293|“자네, 창을 만든다고 했나?”
294|
295|“예?”
296|
297|“귀먹었나? 뭘 자꾸 되물어?”
298|
299|황급히 고개를 들자 퉁명스러운 얼굴의 장태보가 보였다. 그가 말을 이었다.
300|
301|“뭐, 나보고 직접 만들라고 하면 당연히 거절이지만 소개 정도는 시켜 줄 수 있지.”
302|
303|“혹시 제자라는 철기방주…….”
304|
305|“그 자리가 그렇게 한가해 보이나? 그놈도 바빠. 자네 정도면 족히 수년은 기다려야 될 걸세.”
306|
307|“헉, 몇 년씩이나요?”
308|
309|“그럼 병기라는 것이 하루아침에 완성되는 줄 알았나? 나보다는 못해도 한 솜씨 하는 녀석이니 주문도 밀려 있을 게 뻔하지. 가려서 받아도 그 정도야.”
310|
311|아무리 그래도 그렇지, 몇 년이라니.
312|
313|예상치 못한 장기 프로젝트에 숨이 턱 막혔다.
314|
315|“그, 그럼 어떡합니까?”
316|
317|“어떡하긴 뭘 어떡하나? 내가 소개장이라도 써 줄 테니 가져가게. 명색이 사부 소개로 온 놈인데, 조금이라도 빨리 해 주겠지. 그놈이 창 하나는 기똥차게 만들거든.”
318|
319|“오오. 오오오.”
320|
321|“이번에 마적 놈들 때문에 마을이 어수선했는데, 그거 처리한 게 자네라고 들어서 특별히 해 주는 걸세. 거기, 지필묵 있나?”
322|
323|갑자기 지목당한 혁무진이 얼떨떨한 얼굴로 대답했다.
324|
325|“없습니다.”
326|
327|“응. 딱 봐도 안 들고 다니게 생겼어. 그럼 옆에 자네는…….”
328|
329|“쩝, 쩝쩝.”
330|
331|저걸 지금 먹네.
332|
333|객잔에서 싸 온 만두를 볼이 터져라 밀어 넣는 청풍의 모습에 장태보가 한숨을 내쉬었다.
334|
335|“……만두 맛있나?”
336|
337|“쩝쩝. 네.”
338|
339|“매종학 대협이 말년에 이상한 놈을 하나 거뒀군. 그럼 여기서 잠깐 기다려 보게.”
340|
341|늙으면 죽어야지, 요즘 젊은 놈들은 예의를 몰라요.
342|
343|들으라는 듯이 꿍얼거린 장태보가 방 안에서 지필묵을 꺼내왔다.
344|
345|“우선 병장기는 창이고…… 생각해 둔 형태나 무게. 뭐 그런 거 있나?”
346|
347|“아, 넵.”
348|
349|“읊어 보게.”
350|
351|나는 7년간 창을 사용하며 충분히 손에 익은 무게와 형태를 상세하게 설명해 나갔다.
352|
353|그럴 때마다 장태보는 말없이 고개를 끄덕이거나, 아니면 내게 더 적합한 창을 제작할 수 있는 첨언을 덧붙여 주었다.
354|

“Why would I lie? Especially while staking the name of someone as distinguished as the Sword Saint?”

[P60]
“Hah. So he’s the Sword Saint’s successor…”

[P61]
Had that worked? No matter where you went in the world, connections were king: school ties, hometown ties, and blood ties.

[P62]
In the Murim, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s very existence inspired respect and awe.

[P63]
Jang Taebo stared at Cheongpung in evident surprise, then opened his mouth.

[P64]
“So what do you want me to do about it?”

[P65]
“Ah…”

[P66]
“I have nothing to do with Huashan. Well, I did make a sword at the request of the current Sect Leader of Huashan, Heavenly Sword True Person,[^2] about thirty years ago. But that’s all.”

[P67]
He continued firmly.

[P68]
“I’m eighty years old. I’m still in good health, and I’ve accumulated plenty of wealth. As a man who has worked iron all his life, I can proudly say that I rank among the top three in the world.”

[P69]
“That’s why I’m asking you.”

[P70]
“That’s why I’m refusing. I’ve done all the work I care to do. I’ve made enough swords to last me a lifetime.”

[P71]
“I use a spear.”

[P72]
“Oh, did you?”

[P73]
“Yes.”

[P74]
“A spear would take even more work. I’d rather make a sword.”

[P75]
“Elder!”

[P76]
I grabbed Jang Taebo’s hand and gave him an earnest look.

[P77]
“Couldn’t you think of it as something to pass the time and help me just this once?”

[P78]
“When did I say I wouldn’t?”

[P79]
“You’ve been saying that this whole time.”

[P80]
Jang Taebo harshly shook off my hand.

[P81]
“I said I’d help you. If you bring me the Herb of Eternal Youth.”

[P82]
“Oh, please.”

[P83]
“Bring me the gongcheong seokyu and dragon pearl while you’re at it. I hear that when fighting a dragon, you should avoid its tail, circle around behind it, and choke it. I’m telling you so you don’t get hurt.”

[P84]
“…A dragon isn’t a person. How am I supposed to kill it by choking it?”

[P85]
“Then burst its balls.”

[P86]
“What if it’s female?”

[P87]
“See you in the next life.”

[P88]
I had finally met a formidable opponent.

[P89]
His way of screwing with people had been honed over decades. My fists trembled, and the back of my head throbbed.

[P90]
“Are you really going to be like this?”

[P91]
“That is precisely how I’m going to be.”

[P92]
“I didn’t want to go this far…”

[P93]
“Go on. Spit it out.”

[P94]
“Should I spread the word that the former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild lives here?”

[P95]
I was only saying it. Obviously, I had no intention of actually doing it.

[P96]
But Jang Taebo merely grinned at my threat to make his life difficult.

[P97]
“Then I suppose I have no choice. I’ll have to return to the Ironcraft Guild before all sorts of gnats start swarming around.”

[P98]
“Huh?”

[P99]
This wasn’t how it was supposed to go. As I was thinking that, Jang Taebo asked,

[P100]
“If I return to the Ironcraft Guild, what do you think I’ll do?”

[P101]
“…How would I know?”

[P102]
“I’ll devote the rest of my life to making ten weapons. Then I’ll distribute those weapons, each made with all my heart and soul, among the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and have some in-depth conversations with them about the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Your name will come up quite often in particular.”

[P103]
“W-What are you planning to tell them?”

[P104]
“I’ll leave that to your imagination. Oh, and you do know that martial artists will stake their lives on their weapons regardless of how advanced their martial arts are, don’t you? I’m sure they’ll be happy to grant a small request of mine.”

[P105]
“…”

[P106]
It might be a small request to the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but it would be anything but small to me or the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P107]
If he bad-mouthed us with even a few words in front of them, a hit to our reputation would be the least of it. We might even face real pressure from them.

[P108]
“Well, I suppose I should start preparing to leave. Let’s see, what should I pack…?”

[P109]
As he turned to go into his room and pack, I grabbed his wrist. Jang Taebo asked innocently,

[P110]
“What is it?”

[P111]
I lowered my head in defeat.

[P112]
“Please stop. I give up.”

[P113]
“Is that all?”

[P114]
“I’m sorry for acting cocky.”

[P115]
“And?”

[P116]
“I won’t tell anyone that you’re living here.”

[P117]
“Given that you came looking for me like this, it can’t be something only you know, can it?”

[P118]
“I’ll explain everything properly to my eldest brother, too.”

[P119]
“You’re sure?”

[P120]
“Of course.”

[P121]
“Hm. You’re not completely ill-mannered, then.”

[P122]
Having gotten every answer he wanted, Jang Taebo smiled with satisfaction.

[P123]
I had defeated enemies stronger than me time and again, but I couldn’t break the will of an old man enjoying a quiet retirement.

[P124]
*So where am I supposed to have the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron forged?*

[P125]
I’d finally thought I was about to have my first cherished weapon…

[P126]
I was staring dejectedly at the half-chewed, discarded He Shou Wu when Jang Taebo spoke.

[P127]
“You said you were making a spear?”

[P128]
“Pardon?”

[P129]
“Are you deaf? Why do you keep asking me to repeat myself?”

[P130]
I hurriedly raised my head to find Jang Taebo scowling at me. He continued,

[P131]
“Well, if you ask me to make it myself, I’ll obviously refuse. But I can at least give you an introduction.”

[P132]
“You mean the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, your disciple…”

[P133]
“Do you think the Guild Leader has that much time on his hands? He’s busy, too. Even someone like you would have to wait several years at the very least.”

[P134]
“Several years?”

[P135]
“What, did you think a weapon could be completed overnight? He’s not as good as me, but he’s skilled enough that his orders are bound to be backed up. Even picking and choosing which ones to accept, it still takes that long.”

[P136]
Even so, several years?

[P137]
The prospect of such an unexpectedly long project left me short of breath.

[P138]
“T-Then what do I do?”

[P139]
“What do you mean, what do you do? I’ll write you a letter of introduction. Take it with you. You’ll be going there with a recommendation from his master, so he’ll probably finish it a little sooner. That fellow makes one hell of a spear.”

[P140]
“Ooh. Ooooh.”

[P141]
“The village was in an uproar because of those mounted bandits, and I heard you were the one who dealt with them. I’ll do this for you as a special favor. Do you have paper, a brush, and ink?”

[P142]
Hyuk Mujin, suddenly singled out, answered with a bewildered expression,

[P143]
“No.”

[P144]
“Right. One look at you, and I can tell you don’t carry such things. Then what about you…?”

[P145]
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”

[P146]
*He’s eating those now?*

[P147]
Jang Taebo sighed at the sight of Cheongpung stuffing the dumplings we had bought at the inn into his mouth until his cheeks looked ready to burst.

[P148]
“…Are the dumplings good?”

[P149]
“Chomp, chomp. Yes.”

[P150]
“Mae Jonghak took in a strange one in his later years. Fine, wait here a moment.”

[P151]
“Old people should just die. Young people these days have no manners.”

[P152]
Muttering loudly enough for us to hear, Jang Taebo went inside and returned with paper, a brush, and ink.

[P153]
“First, the weapon is a spear… Do you have a particular shape or weight in mind?”

[P154]
“Ah, yes.”

[P155]
“Tell me.”

[P156]
I described in detail the weight and shape that had become thoroughly familiar to me over seven years of wielding a spear.

[P157]
As I spoke, Jang Taebo either nodded silently or offered advice on how to make the spear better suited to me.

[P158]
*He really is an expert.*

[P159]
Sixty years in the trade had not gone to waste.

[P160]
He gave my body a quick once-over, then rattled off one correction after another. He gauged the size of my hands and the length of my arms and legs with uncanny accuracy, then adjusted the thickness and shape of the spear shaft little by little.

[P161]
“All right, this is the last thing. Where are you planning to put the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron? In the spearhead, presumably?”

[P162]
“…?”

[P163]
“Why are you making that face? You said you had Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. You’re not planning to leave it out, are you?”

[P164]
“No, I’m going to use it…”

[P165]
“Do you not have much? By my estimate, ten nyang should be enough to produce something worthy of being called a renowned spear. You could pass it down as a family heirloom without shame.”

[P166]
How much was ten nyang? I still wasn’t used to the unit of weight, so I had no idea.

[P167]
As I hesitated, Jang Taebo barked,

[P168]
“Ah! How much are you going to use?”

[P169]
“That’s… Just a moment.”

[P170]
Seeing was believing. It would be faster to show him.

[P171]
Pretending to rummage through my travel bag, I took the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron from my Inventory and casually held it out.

[P172]
“It’s about this much.”

[P173]
“…”

[P174]
“Elder?”

[P175]
Jang Taebo didn’t answer. He stared intently at the chunk of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, which was larger than a grown man’s head, for a long time before asking in a hoarse voice,

[P176]
“This… This is all Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”

[P177]
“Yes. This isn’t your first time seeing it, is it?”

[P178]
“I-I can’t believe this.”

[P179]
His wrinkled hands trembled faintly. Jang Taebo stroked the cold, blue-tinged Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron as though he had been reunited with a child after sixty years. A sharp light flashed in his eyes.

[P180]
“Entrust it to me.”

[P181]
The old man who had found everything a nuisance was nowhere to be seen. His voice brimmed with passion and vitality.

[P182]
“I’ll make you the greatest divine weapon in the world.”

[P183]
Ding.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

“Mae Jonghak took in a strange one in his later years. Fine, wait here a moment.”

[P151]
“Old people should just die. Young people these days have no manners.”

[P152]
Muttering loudly enough for us to hear, Jang Taebo went inside and returned with paper, a brush, and ink.

[P153]
“First, the weapon is a spear… Do you have a particular shape or weight in mind?”

[P154]
“Ah, yes.”

[P155]
“Tell me.”

[P156]
I described in detail the weight and shape that had become thoroughly familiar to me over seven years of wielding a spear.

[P157]
As I spoke, Jang Taebo either nodded silently or offered advice on how to make the spear better suited to me.

[P158]
*He really is an expert.*

[P159]
Sixty years in the trade had not gone to waste.

[P160]
He gave my body a quick once-over, then rattled off one correction after another. He gauged the size of my hands and the length of my arms and legs with uncanny accuracy, then adjusted the thickness and shape of the spear shaft little by little.

[P161]
“All right, this is the last thing. Where are you planning to put the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron? In the spearhead, presumably?”

[P162]
“…?”

[P163]
“Why are you making that face? You said you had Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. You’re not planning to leave it out, are you?”

[P164]
“No, I’m going to use it…”

[P165]
“Do you not have much? By my estimate, ten nyang should be enough to produce something worthy of being called a renowned spear. You could pass it down as a family heirloom without shame.”

[P166]
How much was ten nyang? I still wasn’t used to the unit of weight, so I had no idea.

[P167]
As I hesitated, Jang Taebo barked,

[P168]
“Ah! How much are you going to use?”

[P169]
“That’s… Just a moment.”

[P170]
Seeing was believing. It would be faster to show him.

[P171]
Pretending to rummage through my travel bag, I took the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron from my Inventory and casually held it out.

[P172]
“It’s about this much.”

[P173]
“…”

[P174]
“Elder?”

[P175]
Jang Taebo didn’t answer. He stared intently at the chunk of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, which was larger than a grown man’s head, for a long time before asking in a hoarse voice,

[P176]
“This… This is all Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”

[P177]
“Yes. This isn’t your first time seeing it, is it?”

[P178]
“I-I can’t believe this.”

[P179]
His wrinkled hands trembled faintly. Jang Taebo stroked the cold, blue-tinged Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron as though he had been reunited with a child after sixty years. A sharp light flashed in his eyes.

[P180]
“Entrust it to me.”

[P181]
The old man who had found everything a nuisance was nowhere to be seen. His voice brimmed with passion and vitality.

[P182]
“I’ll make you the greatest divine weapon in the world.”

[P183]
Ding.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 168

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃168화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|퀘스트
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|[불로초를 찾아서]
 10|
 11|이것은 오직 전설로만 전해지는 영초입니다.
 12|
 13|불로불사, 불로장생을 꿈꾸는 지배자들은 불로초를 찾기 위해 수많은 재물과 인력을 쏟아부었지만, 지금까지 그 누구도 발견하지 못했습니다.
 14|
 15|그러나 당신의 남은 수명이 천 년쯤 된다면 도전해 보는 것도 나쁘지 않습니다.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|등급 : ???
 20|
 21|제한 : 진태경
 22|
 23|임무 : 불로초 습득(미완료)
 24|
 25|보상 : ???
 26|
 27|실패 : ???
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|“안 해!”
 34|
 35|삐빅.
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|- 퀘스트를 거절하셨습니다.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|퀘스트 꼬라지 봐라. 오죽하면 퀘스트 등급도 물음표 처리가 되어 있을까.
 44|
 45|‘뭐? 남은 수명이 천 년쯤 되면 도전해 보는 것도 나쁘지 않아?’
 46|
 47|이게 말이야, 방구야.
 48|
 49|내 어이없는 눈빛에 장태보가 수염을 쓰다듬었다.
 50|
 51|“왜, 못 하겠나?”
 52|
 53|“……이걸 도대체 어떻게 합니까?”
 54|
 55|“그럼 관두게. 하수오는 돌려주고.”
 56|
 57|장태보가 내 손에서 하수오를 휙 낚아채더니 아삭아삭 씹기 시작했다.
 58|
 59|“어, 달다. 역시 오십 년 산이야.”
 60|
 61|“…….”
 62|
 63|“응? 자네들 아직도 거기 있나? 무슨 볼일이라도 있어?”
 64|
 65|“아니, 어르신.”
 66|
 67|“왜?”
 68|
 69|“불로초를 구해 오라는 게 상식적으로 말이나 됩니까?”
 70|
 71|“무림에서 상식을 따지는 놈은 오랜만에 보는군. 천년설삼도 있는데 불로초라고 없을까?”
 72|
 73|“…….”
 74|
 75|제법 그럴듯한데.
 76|
 77|순간 설득당할 뻔했지만 다시 정신을 차렸다. 이 바늘도 안 들어갈 것 같은 노인네를 어떻게든 설득해야 한다.
 78|
 79|“대신 필요하신 게 있다면 뭐든 구해 드리겠습니다. 불로초 같은 거 말고요.”
 80|
 81|“정말인가?”
 82|
 83|“그럼요. 정 안 되면 저희 가문의 힘을 총동원해서라도.”
 84|
 85|“흠. 요새 태원진가의 위세가 대단하다는 건 나도 익히 들어 알고 있지.”
 86|
 87|고개를 끄덕인 장태보가 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“그럼 목이 마르니 공청석유(空靑石油) 한 병 구해 오게.”
 90|
 91|“예?”
 92|
 93|공청석유? 한 방울이면 일 갑자의 공력을 얻는다는 그거?
 94|
 95|쌍욕이 튀어 나가려는 걸 간신히 참았다. 장태보가 실실 웃으며 말을 잇는다.
 96|
 97|“만년한철로 병기를 만든다고 했지? 그럼 검갑도 좋은 걸 써야겠구먼. 내 듣자 하니 저 세상 끝에 용이 있다던데, 발톱 좀 뽑아 오게. 겸사겸사 여의주도 하나 챙겨 오고.”
 98|
 99|띠링.
100|
101|
102|
103|- 퀘스트, [공청석유, 용의 발톱, 여의주 구하기]가 생성되었습니다.
104|
105|
106|
107|퀘스트를 수락하시겠습니까?
108|
109|Y   /   N
110|
111|
112|
113|……하겠냐?
114|
115|속이 부글부글 끓어오르는 걸 느끼며 퀘스트창을 지웠다. 혁무진이 입을 가리고 소곤거렸다.
116|
117|“노인네가 노망 난 것 같은데요?”
118|
119|“다 들린다. 대가리에 피도 안 마른 놈이 못 하는 말이 없구나.”
120|
121|장태보가 솥뚜껑만 한 주먹을 흔들던 그때, 청풍이 손을 번쩍 들고 외쳤다.
122|
123|“저 찾으러 갈래요! 저 시켜 주세요!”
124|
125|“뭐?”
126|
127|“불로초! 공청석유! 용!”
128|
129|드디어 이 구역의 미친놈이 나섰구나.
130|
131|샛별처럼 반짝이는 눈빛과 열정으로 타오르는 몸짓. 청풍의 박력에 장태보가 흠칫 물러섰다.
132|
133|“네놈은 누구냐?”
134|
135|청풍이 씩씩하게 대답했다.
136|
137|“저는 우리 할아버지 손잔데요!”
138|
139|“네놈 조부님이 누군데?”
140|
141|“우리 할아버지신데요!”
142|
143|“……미친놈이로고.”
144|
145|어서 와, 청풍은 처음이지?
146|
147|고개를 절레절레 내젓는 장태보에게 슬쩍 한마디를 던졌다.
148|
149|“혹시 매종학 대협을 아십니까?”
150|
151|“내 비록 무인은 아니나, 일평생을 무림에 발을 담그고 있던 몸일세. 백정들도 아는 검성을 모르겠나?”
152|
153|“저 친구가 그 검성이 직접 키우며 가르친 제자입니다.”
154|
155|“뭐라! 그게 사실인가?”
156|
157|“거짓말해서 뭐 하겠습니까? 그것도 검성씩이나 되는 분의 이름을 걸고.”
158|
159|“허, 검성의 후인이란 말이지…….”
160|
161|먹혔나? 원래 세상 어딜 가나 최고는 학연, 지연, 혈연이다.
162|
163|무림에서 검성 매종학의 존재는 그 자체만으로도 존경과 경의의 대상.
164|
165|사뭇 놀란 표정으로 청풍을 바라보던 장태보가 입을 열었다.
166|
167|“그래서, 뭐 어쩌라고?”
168|
169|“아…….”
170|
171|“나는 화산파와는 아무 연관도 없어. 아니, 삼십여 년 전쯤에 현 화산파 장문인인 천검진인(天劍眞人)의 부탁으로 검을 만들어 준 적이 있긴 하군. 하지만 그뿐일세.”
172|
173|단호한 목소리가 이어졌다.
174|
175|“내 나이가 팔순이야. 이만하면 몸도 정정하고 모아 놓은 재산도 많지. 쇠를 주무르던 사람으로서도 천하에서 세 손가락 안에 들었다고 자부하네.”
176|
177|“그래서 이렇게 부탁드리는 겁니다.”
178|
179|“그래서 이렇게 거절하는 거네. 내가 할 만한 일은 다 끝났어. 검은 질리도록 만들어 봤고.”
180|
181|“저는 창인데요.”
182|
183|“아, 그랬던가?”
184|
185|“예.”
186|
187|“창이라면 손이 더 가겠군. 차라리 검이 나아.”
188|
189|“어르신!”
190|
191|나는 간절한 눈빛으로 정태보의 손을 붙잡았다.
192|
193|“오랜만에 소일거리 하신다고 생각하시고 딱 한 번만 도와주시면 안 됩니까?”
194|
195|“내가 언제 안 된다고 했나?”
196|
197|“방금까지는 안 하신다면서요.”
198|
199|정태보가 모질게 손을 뿌리쳤다.
200|
201|“도와준다니까. 불로초 찾아오면.”
202|
203|“아, 제발요.”
204|
205|“겸사겸사 공청석유와 여의주도 챙겨 오고. 내 듣자 하니 용을 상대할 때는 꼬리를 피해 뒤로 돌아가서 목을 조르면 된다더군. 다치지 말라고 알려 주는 걸세.”
206|
207|“……용이 무슨 사람입니까? 목을 졸라서 죽이게?”
208|
209|“그럼 불알을 터트려.”
210|
211|“암컷이면요?”
212|
213|“다음 생에 만나세.”
214|
215|오랜만에 만난 강적이다.
216|
217|세월로 다져진 사람 엿 먹이는 화법에 주먹이 부르르 떨리고 뒷골이 당겼다.
218|
219|“이러시깁니까?”
220|
221|“이러기일세.”
222|
223|“이렇게까지 하고 싶진 않았는데…….”
224|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
